sections.title: What is CCP LiteLLM?
sections.body: A local FastAPI proxy that speaks the Anthropic Messages API on the wire, but dispatches requests through LiteLLM to any compatible backend — Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, Google Gemini, or Anthropic itself. Point ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL at http://localhost:8082 and Claude Code / Anthropic SDK clients route transparently to your chosen backend.

sections.title: Multi-Provider Routing
sections.body: PREFERRED_PROVIDER selects the backend. BIG_MODEL, SMALL_MODEL, and FRONTIER_MODEL map Claude's sonnet/haiku/opus tiers to concrete deployment names (e.g. sonnet→gpt-4.1, opus→gpt-5.2). For Azure, AZURE_DEPLOYMENT_MAP JSON resolves 22 model-name→deployment-name pairs so each request targets the correct Azure OpenAI deployment.

sections.title: Azure Fallback Architecture
sections.body: When the proxy is configured for Anthropic but the upstream returns 404 (or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is absent), the server automatically retries once against Azure OpenAI using the tier mapping. A _retried_with_azure flag prevents retry loops. Unit tests under tests/ verify the fallback semantics.

sections.title: Management Surfaces
sections.body: Three operator surfaces: (1) ccp-litellm CLI with start/stop/restart/status/log/troubleshoot; (2) a native Swift menu bar app with live status, model config, and login-item toggles; (3) an interactive ccp-switcher Bash TUI for changing tier→model mappings. LaunchAgents auto-start both proxy and menu bar at login.

sections.title: Supply-Chain Security Posture
sections.body: LiteLLM is pinned to >=1.77.7,<1.82.0 in pyproject.toml. This range blocks the malicious 1.82.7 / 1.82.8 releases (TeamPCP credential-stealer, March 2026) while mitigating CVE-2024-6825 (RCE, <1.40.13) and CVE-2024-8984 (DoS, <1.56.2). An incident-response checklist is documented in LITELLM_VULNERABILITY_POLICY.md.
